newsitem.title: CHINA: China launches official magazine on Taiwan ties.
newsitem.headline: China launches official magazine on Taiwan ties.

text.p: China has launched an official magazine to air its views about Taiwan and has used the first issue to call on its rival to follow the model of Hong Kong to achieve reunification, the Xinhua news agency said on Saturday.

The debut issue of the magazine "Cross-Straits Relations" would soon be published with comment from senior Chinese policy makers on Taiwan and discussion of economic ties and other issues, Xinhua said.

The magazine would urge Taiwan, split from the mainland in 1949 after a civil war, to return to the motherland under the "one country, two systems" formula used to win the return of Hong Kong after 156 years of British colonial rule, the agency said.

"Proper handling of Taiwan-related questions in Hong Kong after '97' will... be good for further developing cross-straits relations and finally realising the total reunification of the motherland," Xinhua quoted Chen Yunlin, deputy director of the Taiwan Affairs Office under the State Council, as saying.

Beijing resumed sovereignty over Hong Kong on July 1 and has pledged the territory a high degree of autonomy under the "one country, two systems" formula drawn up by late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

Chinese President Jiang Zemin has said the same arrangement could work to bring Nationalist-held Taiwan back into the family fold, but Taipei insists reunification will come only after the communist-ruled mainland embraces multi-party democracy.

Hong Kong, which became a Special Administrative Region of China from the July 1 takeover, can decide all Taiwan-related affairs itself except those relating to national sovereignty or Taiwan-China ties, Chen told the magazine.

Only if Taiwan acknowledged there was but one China could Taipei and Beijing resume political talks and resolve their differences, Xinhua quoted Tang Shubei, vice-chairman of the Association for Relations across the Taiwan Straits, as saying.
"We once again call on the Taiwan side to truly return to the principle of "one China" to create the necessary conditions and suitable atmosphere for resuming talks," it quoted Tang as saying.

Taiwan has said it wants eventual reunification with the mainland but Beijing has accused Taipei of working to boost its international profile and says it will invade if the island declares independence.
